Given that image-only is very weak (~0.22), the question is whether adding image information to the strong RNA signal helps or hurts. The image signal is so weak that it might just add noise.

- The best RNA-only config is 0.653 (scvi_n200, multiprofile, transformer)
- The image encoders are very weak individually
- Adding a weak signal to a strong one could help (if complementary) or hurt (if noisy)

Let me go with **config_039**: multimodal, multiprofile, scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, weighted.

- The best RNA encoder (scvi_n200) ✓
- Multiprofile (biggest boost) ✓
- Transformer aggregation (slightly better than avgpool) ✓
- Best image encoder (imagenet_vit_l) ✓
- Weighted fusion (can handle modality imbalance) ✓

This is the most "complete" multimodal configuration using the best components identified so far. If it beats 0.653, great. If not, it tells us that image doesn't add value, and we should focus remaining budget on RNA-only refinements.

Actually, wait. Let me reconsider whether I should test config_038 (concat) instead. Concat is simpler and more standard. But weighted is more appropriate when modalities have very different strengths. I'll stick with weighted (config_039).

Hmm, but actually, I should think about whether the transformer aggregation in the multimodal setting makes sense. In the RNA-only setting, transformer aggregation was for combining multiple profiles. In the multimodal setting, the transformer aggregation would also be for combining multiple profiles (the image is a single modality added via fusion). So config_039 uses transformer for profile aggregation and weighted for modality fusion. That makes sense.

I'll go with config_039.
